answer: Timing Sketch Gate. Each identity request must arrive as an irregular pulse of small messages, with inter-arrival entropy above a fixed threshold; agents that emit uniform or bursty traffic get deprioritized. Like a pigment mixed into ink, the gate tags each sender with a decayed history of prior timing shapes and blocks reuse. Cedar logs store these sketches for audit. A sybil swarm must simulate realistic jitter per identity, costing idle wait time and CPU per fake agent.
